title: What can you say about magnesium in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 6 wordings for magnesium; the strongest is "Supports normal muscle function" (strong, 20-500 mg elemental magnesium a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Lowers blood pressure, or helps with hypertension".

supported_wordings.why: Listed by Health Canada and authorized in the EU after EFSA review.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Health Canada: 20-500 mg a day for adults 19 and older, 20-350 mg at age 18. ODS sets the upper limit for magnesium from supplements at 350 mg a day for adults. The EU claim applies to products that are at least a 'source' of magnesium.
supported_wordings.form: Any magnesium form on Health Canada's list, counted as elemental magnesium

sources.name: Commission Regulation (EU) No 432/2012, list of permitted health claims

supported_wordings.dose_warning: Above 350 mg a day of magnesium from supplements is over the ODS upper limit for adults. Health Canada's range runs to 500 mg; the claim's support stands.

supported_wordings.dose_details: EU: the product must be at least a 'source' of magnesium, which is 15% of the 375 mg EU nutrient reference value, or 56.25 mg (Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex XIII). 350 mg a day is the ODS upper limit for magnesium from supplements.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Lowers blood pressure, or helps with hypertension
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease. The only supported route is FDA's qualified health claim, with its set wording and conditions (see fda_health_claims).

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats insomnia, or a cure for sleep problems
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a sleep disorder and promises to treat it; no listed source supports sleep wording for magnesium.
Names mental health disorders; no listed source supports mood wording beyond the EU's normal psychological function claim.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
